topic.title: Installing and configuring hardware sensors
topic.para: The sensors command is part of the sensors package. To read the temperature from the ACPI thermal zones, you do not need the package. For details, see .

step.para: Reboot the system to activate the change.
Check which sensors the kernel already provides:

The output lists the sensors that the kernel has registered, for example, ACPI thermal zones and NVMe drives. For a sample and an explanation, see . If the kernel has registered no sensor, the command reports No sensors found!

Optionally, search for additional hardware monitoring chips that the kernel does not register on its own, for example, on an I2C or SMBus adapter. Do this only if a sensor that you need is missing from the output of sensors.

warning.title: Hardware probing can hang or damage a system
warning.para: The sensors-detect command accesses hardware to identify chips. According to its man page, this can lock up the SMBus and, in rare cases, damage hardware. The man page advises against running the command on production servers.

step.para: If you accept this risk, run the following command:
The --auto option runs the command without interaction and assumes the default answer to every question. Without it, the command asks each question and waits for your answer.
If the command finds a chip, it prints a summary of the chips that it found. Because of the --auto option, it accepts the default answer to the last question:
step.screen:
Now follows a summary of the probes I have just done.
Driver `coretemp': * Chip `Intel digital thermal sensor' (confidence: 9)
Driver `to-be-written': * ISA bus, address 0xa40 Chip `ITE IT8686E Super IO Sensors' (confidence: 9)
Do you want to generate /etc/sysconfig/lm_sensors? (YES/no): Created symlink '/etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/lm_sensors.service' → '/usr/lib/systemd/system/lm_sensors.service'.
step.para: The command generates the file /etc/sysconfig/lm_sensors and enables and starts the lm_sensors service. The unit file of the service is part of the sensors package. To check the status of the service, run:
step.screen: ● lm_sensors.service - Initialize hardware monitoring sensors Loaded: loaded (/usr/lib/systemd/system/lm_sensors.service; enabled; preset: disabled) Active: active (exited) since Mon 2026-09-21 07:40:32 CEST; 16ms ago Invocation: e3f984a1d2cf43528b9b753f1d698a65 Process: 1433 ExecStart=/sbin/modprobe -qab $BUS_MODULES $HWMON_MODULES (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS) Process: 1436 ExecStart=/usr/bin/sensors -s (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS) Main PID: 1436 (code=exited, status=0/SUCCESS) CPU: 34ms
step.para: If the command finds no chip, it reports Sorry, no sensors were detected. It generates no configuration file, and the service stays disabled. The sensors that the sensors command already lists are not affected.
